findings.title: Rejected-email state is shared across controller instances
findings.body: `rejectedEmails` is initialized on the controller definition, so its mutable array can be shared by every `CreateAccountController` instance. If one signup attempt receives an email validation error, that address may remain rejected when another user opens the signup modal, preventing that user from registering with the same address. Initialize the array per controller instance instead.

findings.title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive
findings.body: This query compares the submitted email exactly with the stored value. Email addresses with different casing, such as `Blocked@Example.com` versus `blocked@example.com`, therefore do not match on a case-sensitive database, allowing a user to bypass a block by changing capitalization. Normalize both stored and incoming addresses consistently before lookup (and when creating block records).

findings.title: Concurrent matches can lose match-count increments
findings.body: The method reads `match_count`, increments it in Ruby, and saves the whole record. Two concurrent validations can read the same count and both save the same incremented value, undercounting matches. Use an atomic database increment and update the timestamp atomically so the statistics remain accurate under concurrent signup attempts.
